title: Taal Volcano's gas emissions rise as earthquakes decline

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — Sulfur dioxide emissions from Taal Volcano in Batangas province have increased significantly, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) reported Sunday, Nov. 22. In its latest 24-hour monitoring, Phivolcs recorded 567 metric tons (MT) of sulfur dioxide emissions from the volcano, which it classified as a “weak emission.” The figure marked a sharp increase from the daily average of 215 MT recorded from Nov. 17 to 21. Meanwhile, seismic activity at Taal Volcano has declined, with only three volcanic earthquakes recorded over the past 24 hours, according to the latest Phivolcs bulletin.
